chunks: Notes on the hajj of the Prophets and the Messengers, peace of Allah be upon them all.

2274 - Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام said: “Adam عليه السلام came to this House a thousand times on his two feet; of them, seven hundred were hajj pilgrimages and three hundred were ‘umrah pilgrimages. He used to come to it from the direction of al-Sham, and he used to perform hajj upon a bull. The place where he stayed the night, عليه السلام, was al-Hatim, and it is what lies between the door of the House and the Black Stone. Adam عليه السلام circumambulated before looking at Hawwa’ for one hundred years. And Jibra’il عليه السلام said to him: ‘May Allah greet you with life and favor you,’ meaning: ‘May Allah make you laugh.’”

key_terms.الشَّامِ: the region of al-Sham from which Adam came
key_terms.الْبَيْتَ: the Sacred House, meaning the Ka‘bah
key_terms.الْحَجَرِ الْأَسْوَدِ: the Black Stone of the Ka‘bah
key_terms.الْحَطِيمُ: the area between the door of the House and the Black Stone
key_terms.بَيَّاكَ: a greeting expression here explained as bringing joy

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the hajj of Adam عليه السلام to the Ka‘bah?
ai.summary: This narration describes the repeated hajj and ‘umrah of Adam عليه السلام to the Sacred House and mentions details of his approach, lodging place, and tawaf. It presents the pilgrimage of the early prophets as an established act of worship connected to the Ka‘bah and preserves a report about Jibra’il’s greeting to Adam عليه السلام.
